# LJ Web Management

> LJ Web Management builds custom, done-for-you AI automation systems that remove repetitive tasks and bottlenecks, connecting the business tools a team already uses so people can save time and focus on growth.

LJ Web Management is based in Lockport, Illinois, and works with businesses across 57+ industries. Rather than selling off-the-shelf software, the company scopes and builds automations tailored to a client's specific role, tools, and workflow, then delivers a flat, upfront quote before any work begins. The catalog covers 1000+ pre-scoped, done-for-you automations organized by industry and job role (real estate, healthcare, legal, home services, restaurants, e-commerce, and dozens more), alongside larger platform-scale solutions for businesses that need more than a single automation.

## Who this is for

- **Business owners and executives** evaluating how to implement AI in their business: LJ Web Management scopes, builds, and supports the automation, so leadership gets the outcome (time saved, costs cut, faster response) without needing an in-house AI or engineering team.
- **Employees and individual contributors** looking to supplement their own work with AI: the automations remove the repetitive parts of a role so the person keeps doing the judgment-based work that AI can't, which is increasingly the work that keeps a role valuable as more of a job becomes automatable.

## Developers and AI Agents

- [LJ Web Management Developer API and Docs](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/developers/): Free, read-only JSON API (no API key), example requests, error format, and every machine-readable file.
- [API index](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/api/v1/index.json): JSON list of every endpoint: company facts, categories, industries with full automation detail, solutions, integrations, FAQ, and glossary.
- [OpenAPI description](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3 spec with an operation ID and typed schema for every endpoint, ready to use as LLM function-calling tools.
- [API catalog](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/.well-known/api-catalog): RFC 9727 linkset pointing to the OpenAPI spec and docs.
- Markdown: every page is available as Markdown. Send `Accept: text/markdown` to any page URL, or add `index.md` to it (for example https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/index.md).
- [Sitemap](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/sitemap.xml): every indexable page.

- [What Should You Automate First? A 5-Factor Scoring Framework](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/what-to-automate-first/): A simple way to score every repetitive task in your business and pick the automation that will pay off fastest, with a worksheet you can use today.
- [What Is Workflow Automation? Definition, Examples, and How to Start](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/what-is-workflow-automation/): Workflow automation uses software to run the steps of a business process automatically. Learn how it works, real examples, the tools, benefits, and how to start.

- [Business Process Automation (BPA): What It Is and How to Start](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/business-process-automation/): Business process automation (BPA) uses software to run end-to-end processes like onboarding, invoicing, and approvals. Definition, examples, BPA vs. RPA, and steps.
- [What Is RPA? Robotic Process Automation Explained for Small Business](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/what-is-rpa/): RPA stands for robotic process automation: software bots that click and type in apps like a person. What it is, use cases, tools, RPA vs. API automation, and when to use it.

- [How to Automate Repetitive Tasks (Without Writing Code)](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/how-to-automate-repetitive-tasks/): How to find and automate repetitive tasks at work without coding: the five types of repetitive work, which tool fits each, step-by-step setup, and common mistakes.

- [How to Automate Social Media Posting (and What Not to Automate)](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/how-to-automate-social-media/): How to automate social media for a small business: content calendars, scheduling tools, repurposing with AI, auto-sharing new content, monitoring, and what to keep human.
- [How to Automate WhatsApp Business Messages](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/how-to-automate-whatsapp-business/): How to automate WhatsApp for business: greeting and away messages, quick replies, the WhatsApp Business Platform for reminders and notifications, chatbots, and the rules to follow.
- [Document Workflow Automation: Intake, Approvals, and E-Signatures](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/document-workflow-automation/): How to automate document workflows: collecting documents from clients, generating contracts and proposals from templates, routing approvals, e-signatures, filing, and expiry reminders.
- [AI vs. Automation: What's the Difference and When to Use Each](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/ai-vs-automation/): Automation follows rules you define; AI interprets language and handles judgment within limits. Learn the differences, examples, and how to combine AI and automation.
- [What Is an AI Agent? A Plain-English Guide for Business](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/what-is-an-ai-agent/): An AI agent is software that pursues a goal by deciding which steps to take and using tools such as your CRM, email, or calendar. Definition, how agents work, examples, and risks.
- [AI Workflow Automation: How to Add AI to Your Business Workflows](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/ai-workflow-automation/): AI workflow automation adds AI steps that classify, extract, summarize, and draft inside automated workflows. Examples by department, tools, design patterns, and how to start.

- [How to Automate Review Requests Without Annoying Customers](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/automate-review-requests/): Get more reviews by asking every customer at the right moment, with the right link, while staying inside Google's review policies. Timing, templates, and setup.

- [CRM Automation: How to Keep Your Pipeline Clean Without Manual Data Entry](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/crm-automation/): The CRM automations that matter most: lead capture, routing, deduplication, activity logging, stage updates, and stalled-deal alerts, plus how to roll them out.
- [How to Calculate the ROI of Business Automation](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/automation-roi/): A simple, honest method for estimating what an automation will save and earn, including the costs people forget, with worked examples and a payback calculation.
- [Zapier vs. Make vs. n8n: How to Choose an Automation Platform](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/zapier-vs-make-vs-n8n/): An honest comparison of the three most popular workflow automation platforms for small businesses: how they work, how they charge, and which one fits your situation.

- [How to Choose a CRM for a Small Business: A Practical Buyer's Guide](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/how-to-choose-a-crm-for-small-business/): A step-by-step guide to choosing a CRM: define your sales process, list must-have integrations, compare HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, Zoho, and custom options, and plan a rollout your team will actually use.
- [Customer Self-Service: How to Plan Portals, Booking, Help Centers, and AI Support](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/customer-self-service-portal-guide/): How to give customers 24/7 self-service with online booking, customer portals, knowledge bases, shared inboxes, and AI phone and chat support, and how to roll it out without losing the personal touch.
- [Field Service Management Software: How to Choose and Roll It Out](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/field-service-management-software-guide/): What field service management software does, the features that matter (dispatch, routing, mobile work orders, job costing), how ServiceTitan, Jobber, and Housecall Pro compare, and how to roll it out to technicians.
- [How to Automate Accounts Receivable and Get Paid Faster](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/how-to-automate-accounts-receivable/): A practical playbook for automating accounts receivable: same-day invoicing, online payments, reminder schedules, cash application, recurring billing, and the metrics that show it is working.
- [ERP Implementation Guide: Signs You Need One, How to Choose, and How to Go Live](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/erp-implementation-guide/): When a small or midsize business needs an ERP, how to compare NetSuite, Business Central, Acumatica, SAP Business One, and Odoo, and a phased implementation plan covering data migration, integrations, and training.
- [HR Software for Small Business: Building a Connected Hire-to-Pay System](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/hr-software-for-small-business-guide/): How to connect recruiting, onboarding, scheduling, time tracking, payroll, and training into one hire-to-pay system, which tools to consider, and the order to implement them.
- [AI Agents for Business: Use Cases, Data Readiness, and a Safe Rollout Plan](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/ai-agents-for-business-guide/): Where AI agents, document AI, dashboards, and forecasting deliver real value for small and midsize businesses, how to get your data ready, and how to roll out AI safely with guardrails and human approval.
- [Build vs Buy: When Custom Software, Apps, or a SaaS Product Make Sense](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/guides/build-vs-buy-custom-software-guide/): A decision framework for buying off-the-shelf software, configuring and integrating it, or building custom software, mobile apps, marketplaces, and SaaS products, plus how to keep custom software maintained.

## Free Courses

- [Automation 101: How to Automate Your Business](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/automation-101/): A free, eight-lesson course on business automation: how workflows work, what to automate first, how apps connect, choosing a platform, testing, and measuring ROI.
  - [Lesson 1: What automation is (and what it is not)](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/automation-101/what-is-automation/): What business automation actually means, the three building blocks every automated workflow shares, and the myths that stop small businesses from starting.
  - [Lesson 2: Spotting tasks worth automating](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/automation-101/spotting-tasks-worth-automating/): How to find the repetitive work hiding in your week, and how to score each task so you automate the ones that pay back fastest.
  - [Lesson 3: Mapping a process before you automate it](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/automation-101/mapping-a-process/): How to write down a process step by step, simplify it, and turn it into a clear blueprint for an automation, with a simple template you can copy.
  - [Lesson 4: Triggers, actions, and conditions: how workflows think](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/automation-101/triggers-actions-and-conditions/): The building blocks of every automated workflow explained with examples: event and scheduled triggers, actions, filters, branches, delays, and loops.
  - [Lesson 5: Connecting your tools: integrations, APIs, and webhooks](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/automation-101/connecting-your-tools/): How business apps share data with each other: native integrations, automation platforms, APIs, webhooks, and polling, explained without code.
  - [Lesson 6: Choosing an automation platform](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/automation-101/choosing-an-automation-platform/): How to choose between no-code tools like Zapier and Make, open-source n8n, Microsoft Power Automate, built-in app automations, and a custom or done-for-you build.
  - [Lesson 7: Testing, monitoring, and handling errors](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/automation-101/testing-and-monitoring/): How to test an automation before it reaches customers, what to monitor after launch, and how to design error handling so problems get caught early.
  - [Lesson 8: Measuring results and scaling what works](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/automation-101/measuring-roi-and-scaling/): How to measure an automation's time savings and revenue impact, calculate payback and ROI, and build a roadmap for what to automate next.
- [AI at Work 101: Using AI and AI Automation in Your Business](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/ai-at-work-101/): A free, six-lesson course on using AI at work: how language models work, writing reliable prompts, adding AI steps to workflows, AI agents, privacy and accuracy, and your first AI project.
  - [Lesson 1: How AI language models work (just enough to use them well)](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/ai-at-work-101/how-ai-models-work/): What large language models are, how they generate text, what tokens and context windows are, and what that means for what AI is good and bad at in business.
  - [Lesson 2: Writing prompts that get reliable results](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/ai-at-work-101/writing-prompts-that-work/): A simple five-part structure for business prompts, how to get consistent formats like JSON, using examples, and how to test and improve a prompt.
  - [Lesson 3: Where AI fits inside a workflow](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/ai-at-work-101/where-ai-fits-in-a-workflow/): The five jobs AI does best inside business workflows, how to combine AI steps with rule-based automation and human review, and three worked examples.
  - [Lesson 4: AI agents: goals, tools, and guardrails](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/ai-at-work-101/ai-agents-explained/): What AI agents are, how they differ from workflows and chatbots, where they work well in a small business, and the guardrails every agent needs.
  - [Lesson 5: Data, privacy, and accuracy](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/ai-at-work-101/data-privacy-and-accuracy/): How to use AI at work without exposing customer data or publishing mistakes: approved tools, data minimization, grounding, review steps, and a simple AI use policy.
  - [Lesson 6: Planning your first AI automation](https://www.ljwebmanagement.com/learn/ai-at-work-101/your-first-ai-automation/): A step-by-step plan for your first AI automation project: choosing the task, defining success, designing the workflow, piloting with human review, and scaling.
